description: Concurrent flows add the same knowledge-base or wisdom file, so their pull requests conflict add/add. Stage 5 promotion (knowledge/wisdom.py persist_kb_fact and persist_wb_rule, with _build_wisdom_heuristic_item) writes JSON files named by a context-fingerprint hash, and each file carries values that differ per run: created_ts and updated_ts taken from the wall clock, and evidence counters such as total_executions and wilson_lower. Two flows that promote the same context each add the same path with different bytes. On 2026-11-26 two open pull requests both added holon-knowledge/wisdom/heuristics/WB-heuristic-84a6ddeb.json and each later merge needed a conflict pass, a push and a CI cycle.
goal: Make a promoted knowledge-base or wisdom file for a given id byte-identical no matter which flow, run or time writes it, so two flows adding the same path never conflict. Keep run-varying values (wall-clock timestamps, execution counters, Wilson bounds, advisory text that embeds counters) out of the persisted KB/WB file content: derive any timestamp field from a stable value (for example a fixed epoch or the id's fingerprint) or drop it, and keep the counters only where they already live outside these files (the action index database and the ledgers). The file is still written only when absent, and existing files on main stay readable by load_index and by every reader. Put new logic in a small new module if wisdom.py would otherwise grow; do not raise any module line budget.
rationale: Per-flow add/add conflicts on hash-named KB/WB files cost a resolver pass, a push, a CI cycle and a rerun for every second concurrent flow; making the bytes deterministic removes the conflict at its source instead of resolving it afterwards.
acceptance_criteria: Calling persist_kb_fact twice for the same id with different clock times and different evidence counters, in two separate directories, writes byte-identical files; the same holds for persist_wb_rule; each has a test.

Promoting the same context fingerprint from two separate hermetic tmp_path knowledge directories with different execution counts produces byte-identical KB pattern and WB heuristic files; a test asserts this.
A file that already exists is never rewritten, and load_index still reads both the new files and a legacy file that carries created_ts, updated_ts and counters; both are tested.

No test or code change touches the knowledge files under holon-knowledge, the ledgers, or any other module; holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json is unchanged and every module stays within its budget.
'uv run pytest' on the changed and added tests, 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.
